question:
A 52-year-old woman presents with fatigue, difficulty swallowing solid foods, and frequent choking spells. She says her symptoms gradually onset 3 months ago and have progressively worsened. Past medical history is unremarkable. She reports drinking alcohol occasionally but denies smoking or illicit drug use. Her vital signs include: temperature 36.6°C (97.8°F), blood pressure 115/72 mm Hg, pulse 82/min. Physical examination shows conjunctival pallor but is otherwise unremarkable. Laboratory results are significant for the following:
Hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL
Red cell count 2.5 million/mm3
Mean corpuscular volume 73 μm3
Serum ferritin 9.7 ng/mL
A barium swallow study is performed, which shows a proximal esophageal web. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Fatigue, difficulty swallowing solid foods, and choking spells" -> "Gradual onset and progressive worsening over 3 months" -> "No smoking or illicit drug use" -> "Occasional alcohol consumption" -> "Conjunctival pallor on physical examination" -> "Hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL, Red cell count 2.5 million/mm3, MCV 73 μm3, Serum ferritin 9.7 ng/mL" -> "Proximal esophageal web on barium swallow study" -> "Plummer-Vinson syndrome" -> 95%
analysis: The patient's presentation with fatigue, difficulty swallowing solid foods, and frequent choking spells along with the laboratory findings of microcytic anemia (low hemoglobin, low red cell count, low mean corpuscular volume) and low serum ferritin levels suggest iron deficiency anemia. The presence of a proximal esophageal web on barium swallow study is characteristic of Plummer-Vinson syndrome, which is a rare condition associated with iron deficiency anemia and esophageal webs.
